Which revision wins moves the published figures. Under the declared rule, 65 orders that were once cancelled count as delivered revenue because a later revision says delivered. A reader may not expect that of a cancelled order, and neither the report nor any caveat says it.
The report says the export's repeats were deduplicated but never says which revision wins. The only artifact that names the rule, analysis/answers/R02.json, names the wrong one.

The analysis plan assumes independent observations for both hypotheses, but the 44531 orders come from 4198 pseudonymous customers, about 10.6 orders each and up to 23. CLM-TEST-CHANNEL-AOV and the metrics channel_aov_test_* give their population as all orders by channel, but the test runs on delivered orders only (n 17818 and 12055), as the analysis plan registers.

The report and dashboard print 'p 0.0000' for both registered tests. The recomputed p values are about 3e-157 for completion and below double precision for AOV, and a reader may take 0.0000 as exactly zero rather than below 0.0001.

Dashboard cards carry no population field and no confidence level. The test cards show p, statistic and effect with no hypothesis id, alpha, correction or group sizes, so any page-level context there comes from caveat strings alone.
